title: Demand stays durable because four end-market needs keep pulling temperature-controlled logistics capacity
subtitle: Different demand pools reinforce the same requirement: reliable refrigerated transport and cold storage across food, pharma, modern retail, and quick-commerce flows.

blocks.title: Food loss reduction anchors a large, recurring cold-chain use case
blocks.body: Perishable categories need controlled handling from harvest through distribution. Evidence focus: spoilage reduction, shelf-life protection, and broader reach into non-local markets.

blocks.title: Pharma compliance requires validated temperature control across lanes
blocks.body: Vaccines, biologics, and specialty drugs require monitored storage and transport. Evidence focus: compliance-led demand, lower tolerance for excursions, and premium service requirements.

blocks.title: Modern retail expansion raises the need for scheduled replenishment
blocks.body: Organized grocery and foodservice formats depend on dependable cold storage and store delivery. Evidence focus: higher SKU breadth, tighter replenishment cadence, and multi-city distribution.

blocks.title: Quick-commerce service levels intensify demand for proximate cold capacity
blocks.body: Rapid delivery models need inventory positioned close to demand and moved in small, frequent drops. Evidence focus: urban node density, tighter service windows, and higher uptime expectations.
